title: Recurring individual leakers
disclaimer: Archive-based reliability signal, not a guarantee. A person can be accurate on one claim and wrong on another; repeated coverage of the same post is not independent confirmation.

leakers.name: Steve Hemmerstoffer
leakers.note: Appears repeatedly behind early S22, S23, S25 and S27 design renders. The archive treats CAD as useful shape evidence, not a final production blueprint. His S27 and S27 Ultra CAD sets currently disagree with Ice Universe about the Ultra's rear camera treatment, so neither reading is treated as settled. On 28 September 2026 he posted an updated S27 Ultra rear render placing the telephoto at the top of the pill and the flash at the bottom, and noted that early case molds had missed the rear microphone cutout; Ice Universe and two other accounts dispute that order.

references.title: S27 and S27 Ultra CAD renders
Updated S27 Ultra rear camera render

leakers.name: Ice Universe
leakers.note: Frequently attributed across the S22, S23 Ultra and S27 records for camera, display, battery and chipset claims. In August 2026 the account posted a camera-plateau sketch and case images for the S27 Pro and Ultra that conflict with the OnLeaks CAD camera bar; the archive preserves both and treats neither as confirmed. On 14 September 2026 it rejected the reported 4x 1/1.9-inch telephoto as false and said the Ultra keeps its 5x 1/2.52-inch module, while leaving the previously asserted removal of the 3x shooter unaddressed. On 24 September 2026 the account posted that the Galaxy S27 Ultra will pick up Xiaomi's split-screen privacy behaviour, protecting one app in a two-app view while the other stays visible; every readable account of that claim in this archive traces back to this single post, so it is recorded as one report rather than as corroboration. Individual claims still need separate verification. On 29 September 2026 the account posted that the Ultra drops its 10MP 3x telephoto and keeps the 5x module alone, that the 200MP main camera moves to an ISOCELL HP6 and that colour and highlight handling change; the archive records those as one post relayed widely, not as independent confirmation. On 30 September it gave 218 g and 7.9 mm for the Ultra and shared a third-party screen-protector image, and it separately disputed OnLeaks' updated camera-layout render, saying the telephoto sits at the bottom. On 5 October 2026 the account posted that the Galaxy S27 Ultra's base colours are Black, Blue, Light Pink and White and added a special Violet later the same day; Android Authority, 9to5Google, SamMobile and Sammy Fans relayed the post within a day, so the archive records one tipster post rather than four witnesses, and no shade, finish or market detail was given. On 15 October 2026 the account gave 1.28 mm display bezels and a 4.69 mm camera bump for the Galaxy S27 Ultra; GSMArena read that as thicker than the S26 Ultra's 1.15 mm bezels while SamMobile and Gizmochina read it as slimmer against 1.32 mm, so the archive records the measurements and the disagreement about the baseline, not a direction. On 17 October it posted a video of another S27 Ultra case showing the same horizontal camera bar, and Sammy Fans relayed it; the post was not read.

leakers.name: Evan Blass
leakers.note: The S25 archive records additional renders attributed to him, making him a notable source for official-looking pre-launch imagery rather than a general specification oracle.

leakers.name: Yogesh Brar
leakers.note: Named in S23 reporting for camera and chipset specifications. The archive keeps his claims distinct from later launch confirmation.

leakers.name: Ross Young
leakers.note: The S23 archive cites him for an early limited-color prediction. This is a narrower signal than a complete device specification leak.

leakers.name: Roland Quandt
leakers.note: The S23 archive attributes apparent Snapdragon marketing and comparison material to him. In September 2026 two outlets credited him with the claim that the Galaxy S27 Ultra keeps a 50-megapixel Sony 5x telephoto instead of moving to a 4x module, which lines up with Ice Universe's separate rebuttal of the 4x report. Only the secondary attributions were read here, so this record does not treat outlet coverage as his own verification. Material provenance matters more than the outlet repeating it.

leakers.name: Tron
leakers.note: Named by Notebookcheck in the early S22 Exynos/AMD and Snapdragon regional specification trail. The archive records the regional uncertainty rather than treating it as certainty.

leakers.name: Jukanlosreve
leakers.note: The S25 record attributes leaked S25+ hands-on images to this account, including the camera rings and US mmWave antenna.

leakers.name: Sonny Dickson
leakers.note: The S27 record attributes a wide camera-plateau image report to him. The archive treats image interpretation, such as possible Qi2 magnets, as unconfirmed.

leakers.name: Anthony
leakers.note: The S27 record attributes several early camera, display and chipset claims to this account, but the underlying posts were not independently preserved; it is listed for traceability, not endorsement. In October 2026 Android Headlines named the account among those placing the Ultra's telephoto at the bottom of the camera pill, against the OnLeaks render. On 13 October 2026 Sammy Fans attributed a price roadmap to this account — $1,099, $1,199, $1,399 and $1,499 for the S27, S27+, S27 Pro and S27 Ultra — which contradicts the 8 October @phonefuturist ladder; the post itself was not read, and SammyGuru repeated the figures without naming the account.

leakers.name: Setsuna Digital
leakers.note: Credited by Gizmochina for the earliest S27 S Pen-slot rumor currently located in the archive. One early report is not enough to establish a reliability record.

leakers.name: kro
leakers.note: On 2 September 2026 posted Galaxy S27 Edge figures — a 5.8-inch display, a low-4 mm body and a 4,300 mAh battery — without stating a source, and a second X account contradicted the size the same day. A single uncorroborated post is not a reliability record, so the archive lists the account for traceability only. In late August 2026 the same account was credited with a Galaxy S27 Ultra prototype that dropped the S Pen slot for a 7,000 mAh cell, later reported as settling on a 5,700-6,000 mAh target; that claim was also read only through relays. Between 29 September and 2 October 2026 the account was credited with an Exynos-powered Galaxy S27 Ultra prototype in testing, a claim that Snapdragon negotiations may have fallen through, a Geekbench 6 single-core score near 3,900 for the Exynos 2700, and the counter-reading that the Ultra's telephoto sits at the bottom of the camera pill; every one of those was read only through relays.

leakers.name: SPYGO19726
leakers.note: Replied to the S27 Edge post on 2 September 2026 with a different size — 6.8 inches at 5.4 mm — and no stated source, without disputing the battery figure. The archive has one appearance for this account and treats it as unproven.

leakers.name: Lanzuk
leakers.handle: Naver blog account, reported also as yeux1122
leakers.focus: Battery chemistry, memory and storage planning
leakers.note: A July 2026 report attributed to this account said silicon-carbon batteries would reach the Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra at roughly 10% more capacity than their S26 equivalents, that the base model was undecided on cost and that the chemistry currently degrades faster than lithium-ion. The archive located the claim only through a secondary relay and has not read the original post. On 22 September 2026 Android Authority attributed the whole family's memory and storage configurations to this account writing on the Korean blog Naver, citing Weibo posts and Korean industry sources, and Gagadget reproduced a 24 September post by Tarun Vats that credits Lanzuk and calls the account yeux1122. That alias comes from the relay rather than from a page this archive read at source, and no original post was read. On 30 September 2026 a Naver post attributed to this account, and reported under the alias yeux1122, said the whole S27 line rises in price with steeper steps between storage tiers; 9to5Google and Android Authority relayed it without reading an original post. On 9 October 2026 a Naver post attributed to this account, read only through relays, said Samsung has no plans to put the Exynos 2700 in the Galaxy S27 Ultra in any market, keeping Snapdragon worldwide for the Ultra while the base, Plus and Pro take the Exynos 2700 in most of Europe, Asia and Africa. That sits against the earlier prototype reports the same relays had carried.

references.title: S27 family memory and storage configurations

leakers.name: Abhishek Yadav
leakers.focus: Regulatory filings, UWB and charging specifications
leakers.note: Relayed the China 3C registry listing behind the reported 25 W and 45 W Galaxy S27 and S27 Plus charging speeds. The firmer evidence is the regulatory listing rather than the relay, and this archive did not inspect the registry entry itself. On 16 October 2026 Android Authority, SamMobile and GSMArena attributed to this account the reading of Chinese MIIT entries in which only the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra list ultra-wideband support, leaving the base and Plus without it. That is a second regulatory-filing claim from the same account, which is why the archive moves it from low to medium; the entries were still read only through relays, the model-number mapping is the tipster's, and a missing feature in a filing is weaker than a listed one.

leakers.name: phonefuturist
leakers.focus: Pre-production camera, display and pricing claims
leakers.note: On 31 August 2026 the account was credited with Samsung testing a shared 3x telephoto across the S27 lineup and a single 50-megapixel 1/1.9-inch 4x telephoto for the Ultra, with five Ultra prototypes built and a hardware decision expected around 9 September. Ice Universe later rejected the 4x part. The posts were not read directly and nothing was published with them, so the account is listed for traceability only. On 8 October 2026 a post by the account carried the family's expected United States and global prices - $899, $1,099, $1,299 and $1,399 in the US, a tier higher elsewhere - alongside an M14+ and M16 OLED split for the same four models. 9to5Google, Sammy Fans, Trusted Reviews and PhoneArena relayed it; neither the post nor the Android Headlines page carrying it was read here.

leakers.name: GalaxyFlash2025
leakers.note: In early September 2026 the account was reported to claim the Galaxy S27 Ultra would drop both the 3x and 5x cameras for a single 4x 1/1.9-inch sensor. Ice Universe dismissed that reading as false, and the archive has one appearance for the account, so it is unproven.

leakers.name: WalleGalaxy
leakers.focus: Camera software, charging and display claims
leakers.note: In mid-September 2026 the account claimed the Galaxy S27 Ultra gains updated Samsung Log and APV support for wider dynamic range and a reworked photo pipeline tuned for warmer, more natural colour. Android Authority relayed the claims while stating that the account is not an established source, and this archive agrees: one appearance, no evidence published, listed for traceability only. On 21 September 2026 SammyGuru attributed the family's ten memory and storage configurations to this account, including a possible 128GB tier outside most markets; that relay carries no evidence beyond the account's own claim. On 5 October 2026 Android Authority credited the account with the claim that the Galaxy S27 Ultra keeps its 60 W charging ceiling while sustaining roughly 55-56 W for longer, worth about 2% to 3% in charge time; the post was not read, and Tech Advisor's 8 October round-up carries the same figures under a source list naming phonefuturist and Ice Universe instead. On 10 October 2026 GSMArena, SammyGuru and PhoneArena relayed a claim attributed to this account that the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra will support DC dimming, likely in a hybrid scheme that keeps PWM at low brightness. No panel document or Samsung statement supports it, and the account remains low-signal here: a technical claim is not evidence.

leakers.name: Tarun Vats
leakers.focus: Relaying Korean supply-chain memory and storage claims
leakers.note: On 24 September 2026 posted the Galaxy S27 family's RAM and storage configurations and credited Lanzuk for them. The account relays rather than originates, so its posts add reach rather than independent confirmation, and this archive read the post only through Gagadget's reproduction. One appearance is not a reliability record.

leakers.name: Sawyergalox
leakers.note: On 12 October 2026 SammyGuru attributed to this account a second-generation Privacy Display for the Galaxy S27 Ultra, and possibly the Pro, with better viewing angles, resolution and clarity while the filter is active. The post was not read and no document or specification was cited; the account appears once in this archive and is listed for traceability only. It is not the same account as Anthony (@TheGalox_).
